de: Mitleid haben mit, sich erbarmen, aus Mitleid helfen
sentence: The farmer ____ pity on the hungry stranger and gave him food.
plain: The farmer felt sorry for the hungry stranger and gave him food.
note: take pity on s.o.

de: sich distanzieren von, sich lossagen von, sich abgrenzen von
sentence: The minister tried to ____ himself from the scandal.
plain: The minister tried to show that he had nothing to do with the scandal.
note: Auch: disassociate. Formell.

sentence: There's no use ____ over what happened.
plain: There's no use worrying again and again about what happened.
note: Auch: brood on sth.

prompt: to disappoint someone
sentence: I'm sorry to ____ you down but I won't be able to see you tonight.
plain: I'm sorry to disappoint you but I won't be able to see you tonight.
note: Vergangenheit: let down (unverändert). Nomen: a let-down = eine Enttäuschung.

prompt: to fall asleep
sentence: I was absolutely exhausted and ____ out almost as soon as I sat down.
plain: I was absolutely exhausted and fell asleep almost as soon as I sat down.
note: Umgangssprachlich. Auch: aus einem Wettbewerb ausscheiden (crash out of the cup).

prompt: the person who is responsible for or controls something
sentence: I'd like to speak to the Manager or the person in ____ of customer service please.
plain: I'd like to speak to the manager or the person who is responsible for customer service please.
note: in charge of + Bereich. Auch: take charge of, put s.o. in charge. Nicht verwechseln mit free of charge.

prompt: to wind a recording quickly forward
sentence: Could you ____ forward the cassette to the next song please?
plain: Could you move the cassette quickly forward to the next song please?
note: Auch als Verb mit Bindestrich: fast-forward. Gegenteil: rewind.

de: regelmäßig; auf Teilzeitbasis; auf welcher Grundlage
prompt: one word fits all three: on a regular ____ / on what ____ / on a part-time ____
sentence: Karen goes swimming on a regular ____ as she likes to keep fit.
plain: Karen goes swimming regularly as she likes to keep fit.
note: Weitere Sätze: On what ____ are you claiming the company has made progress? / He is going to return to work on a part-time ____ until he is fully recovered. Plural: bases.

prompt: adverb from PUBLIC
sentence: She rarely speaks ____ about her private life.
plain: She rarely talks in front of everyone about her private life.
note: Schreibweise: publicly, nicht publically. Verwandt: public, publicity, publication.

prompt: noun from PUBLIC: attention from the media
sentence: They were only a small company and tried many different ways of getting free ____ in the local newspaper.
plain: They were only a small company and tried many different ways of getting free attention in the local newspaper.
note: Nicht zählbar: free publicity, bad publicity. Falle: ES publicidad und FR publicité heißen Werbung (EN advertising).

prompt: noun from PUBLISH: the act of making something available to the public
sentence: The book is expected to be ready for ____ at the end of the year.
plain: The book is expected to be ready to be printed and sold at the end of the year.
note: Von publish. ready for publication, on publication.

prompt: noun from DISCIPLINE: a person who believes in strict rules and punishment
sentence: He's a real ____ and believes in being strict with his children.
plain: He believes in strict rules and punishment for his children.
note: Typisch: a strict disciplinarian.

prompt: adjective from DISCIPLINE: relating to punishment for breaking rules
sentence: The company have been criticised for not having a good ____ procedure.
plain: The company have been criticised for not having a good procedure for dealing with rule-breaking.
note: Typisch: disciplinary procedure, disciplinary action, disciplinary hearing.

prompt: adjective from DISCIPLINE: able to control yourself and follow rules
sentence: The soldiers were very ____ and were praised for their attitude.
plain: The soldiers behaved very well and obeyed the rules, and were praised for their attitude.
note: Gegenteil: undisciplined.

prompt: noun from DEVOTE: great love or loyalty
sentence: She always showed a great deal of ____ to her job and worked incredibly hard.
plain: She always showed great loyalty to her job and worked incredibly hard.
note: devotion to + Person oder Aufgabe.

prompt: noun from DEVOTE: a person who loves something very much
sentence: I've always been a ____ of his films and have seen almost every one.
plain: I've always been a big fan of his films and have seen almost every one.
note: devotee of + Thema.

prompt: adverb from DEVOTE
sentence: He supported his team ____, even after they were relegated.
plain: He supported his team loyally, even after they were relegated.
note: relegated = abgestiegen. Verwandt: devote, devoted, devotion.

prompt: to tidy
sentence: If you've finished playing with those toys could you ____ them all away please.
plain: If you've finished playing with those toys, could you tidy them all, please?
note: Pronomen stehen in der Mitte: clear them away. Mit Nomen auch: clear away the plates. Auch: clear up = aufräumen, Ordnung machen.

de: jdn. einweihen, jdn. ins Vertrauen ziehen
prompt: to tell someone about something that is a secret
sentence: I wish you would let me ____ on the big joke. I haven't got a clue what you're all laughing about.
plain: I wish you would tell me about the big joke. I haven't got a clue what you're all laughing about.
note: Gegenstück: be in on sth. = eingeweiht sein (I wasn't in on the plan). Pronomen stehen in der Mitte: let me in on it.

prompt: verb from LONG: to make something longer
sentence: I need to ____ those trousers. They're up past your ankles.
plain: I need to make those trousers longer. They're up past your ankles.
note: Auch ohne Objekt: The days lengthen in spring. Gegenteil: shorten. Verwandt: long, length, lengthy.

prompt: adjective from LONG: lasting a long time, often too long
sentence: He's just written a very ____ report into the amount of absenteeism in the company this year.
plain: He's just written a very long report into the amount of absenteeism in the company this year.
note: Oft mit leicht kritischem Unterton: a lengthy delay, a lengthy process, a lengthy report. Schreibweise: lengthy, nicht lengthly. Auch: at length = ausführlich.

prompt: comparative of LONG: used with not or no to talk about time
sentence: I'm sorry, I can't wait any ____. I'll come back later.
plain: I'm sorry, I have no more time to wait. I'll come back later.
note: can't wait any longer = nicht länger warten können. Vor dem Verb steht no longer (I no longer work here). Auch: not ... any more.

prompt: noun from CONFINE: the state of being kept in a closed place
sentence: The prisoner was kept in solitary ____ for most of his time in jail.
plain: The prisoner was kept alone in a locked cell for most of his time in jail.
note: Typisch: solitary confinement = Einzelhaft. Verwandt: confine, confined, confines.

prompt: plural noun from CONFINE: the limits of a place
sentence: You must stay within the ____ of the camp and not leave without permission.
plain: You must stay inside the limits of the camp and not leave without permission.
note: Fast immer Plural: within the confines of the camp, the law, the room. Das Nomen wird auf der ersten Silbe betont, das Verb confine auf der zweiten.

de: eingesperrt, beschränkt, an einen Ort gebunden
prompt: adjective from CONFINE: kept in a small space or limited to one place
sentence: The weather was terrible and we spent the whole weekend ____ to our room.
plain: The weather was terrible and we had to spend the whole weekend inside our room.
note: be confined to + Ort oder Zustand: confined to bed, to one's room, to a small area. Auch: a confined space = ein enger Raum.

prompt: plural noun from ADJUST: small changes made to improve something
sentence: I need to make one or two ____ to the mechanism before it's finished.
plain: I need to make one or two small changes to the mechanism before it's finished.
note: make adjustments to sth. = etwas nachstellen, nachjustieren. Auch: a period of adjustment = Eingewöhnungszeit. Verwandt: adjust, adjustable.

prompt: adjective from ADJUST: able to be changed to suit different needs
sentence: The back of the chair is ____ and you can lie back as far as you wish to go.
plain: The back of the chair can be moved into different positions and you can lie back as far as you wish to go.
note: Typisch: an adjustable seat, spanner, height, mortgage rate. Endung -able, nicht -ible.

prompt: verb from ADJUST, here with -ing: to get used to a new situation
sentence: I found it very difficult ____ to life in another country.
plain: I found it very difficult to get used to life in another country.
note: adjust to sth. = sich an etwas gewöhnen, sich auf etwas einstellen. Danach Nomen oder -ing: adjust to life abroad, adjust to living alone.

prompt: to support or agree with an idea or plan
sentence: All those ____ favour of the new proposals, please vote now.
plain: All those who support the new proposals, please vote now.
note: in favour of + Nomen oder -ing: in favour of the plan, in favour of staying. Amerikanisch: favor. Gegenteil: be against. Auch: vote in favour of, come out in favour of.

de: sich austauschen, Erfahrungen oder Eindrücke vergleichen
prompt: to exchange ideas, opinions or experiences with someone
sentence: Before we go into the meeting let's get together first and ____ notes.
plain: Before we go into the meeting let's get together first and discuss what each of us thinks.
note: compare notes (with s.o.) (on sth.): sich über Erfahrungen oder Eindrücke austauschen, nicht nur über geschriebene Notizen. Nicht verwechseln: take notes = mitschreiben, make a note of sth. = sich etwas notieren.

de: an jdn. denken, jdm. einen Gedanken widmen
prompt: one word fits three phrases (1/3): to think kindly about someone who is worse off
sentence: If you think it's cold in here ____ a thought for Tim, who's working outside in the snow.
plain: If you think it's cold in here, think about Tim, who's working outside in the snow.
note: Oft als Aufforderung: Spare a thought for ... = Denk auch an jemanden, dem es schlechter geht. Dasselbe Wort passt in spare the time und spare no expense.

de: Zeit erübrigen, sich Zeit nehmen können
prompt: one word fits three phrases (2/3): to have enough free time to give to something
sentence: I'm afraid I can't ____ the time at present as I'm really busy.
plain: I'm afraid I haven't got any free time at present as I'm really busy.
note: Meist verneint oder als Frage: I can't spare the time. Can you spare a minute? Auch: time to spare = übrige Zeit.

de: keine Kosten scheuen, an nichts sparen
prompt: one word fits three phrases (3/3): to spend as much money as needed to make something very good
sentence: The company usually host very nice conferences and ____ no expense when it comes to the food.
plain: The company usually host very nice conferences and spend as much money as needed when it comes to the food.
note: Auch: spare no effort = keine Mühe scheuen. Auch: spare s.o.'s feelings = jdn. schonen.

prompt: to better
sentence: I think the challenger will find it very difficult to improve ____ his last score.
plain: I think the challenger will find it very difficult to do better than his last score.
note: improve on one's best = die eigene Bestleistung übertreffen. Ohne on heißt improve nur besser werden.

prompt: adjective from SMOKE: full of smoke
sentence: I don't like going to the pub as it gets too ____.
plain: I don't like going to the pub as the air gets too full of smoke.
note: a smoky room, smoky bacon (rauchig im Geschmack). Schreibweise: smoky, auch smokey als Name.

prompt: -ing form of SMOKE: used in signs
sentence: I'm afraid this is a no-____ compartment.
plain: I'm afraid you may not smoke in this compartment.
note: no-smoking area, sign, compartment. Auch: non-smoking.

prompt: noun from SMOKE: a person who smokes
sentence: He's a very heavy ____ and suffers from an awful cough.
plain: He smokes a great deal and suffers from an awful cough.
note: a heavy smoker, a chain-smoker, a non-smoker.

prompt: to go ____ (adverb)
sentence: The meeting went very ____ and I'm quite confident they'll sign the contract.
plain: The meeting went very well and I'm quite confident they'll sign the contract.
note: Auch: run smoothly, go without a hitch. Gegenteil: not go according to plan.

prompt: to fall asleep
sentence: After a hard day at work I regularly ____ off in front of the TV in the evening.
plain: After a hard day at work I regularly fall asleep in front of the TV in the evening.
note: Meist ungeplant und kurz: einnicken. Ähnlich: doze off = eindösen. Hier sind fall off und go off falsch.

prompt: adverb from ESSENCE
sentence: We have different views on the subject but ____ we both agree that something needs to be done.
plain: We have different views on the subject but basically we both agree that something needs to be done.
note: essentially = basically; leitet die Kernaussage ein. Verwandt: in essence.

prompt: plural noun from ESSENCE: things you must have
sentence: When you're packing to go away, always make sure you've got the ____ like your passport and money.
plain: When you're packing to go away, always make sure you've got the most important things like your passport and money.
note: the essentials, the bare essentials = das Allernötigste.

prompt: adjective from ESSENCE
sentence: It's ____ that you arrive on time as some very important people are attending the meeting.
plain: It's very important that you arrive on time as some very important people are attending the meeting.
note: It is essential that you arrive ... (auch be, should arrive). Stärker als important.

de: Zweifel an etwas wecken, etwas infrage stellen
prompt: to ____ doubt
sentence: I don't want to ____ doubt on his ability but are we sure he's the best person for the job?
plain: I don't want to question his ability but are we sure he's the best person for the job?
note: cast doubt on/upon sth. Gleichbedeutend: throw doubt on. Auch: raise doubts about.

prompt: adjective from FREQUENCY
sentence: He's a ____ visitor to our restaurant and often arrives with famous celebrities.
plain: He visits our restaurant regularly and often arrives with famous celebrities.
note: a frequent visitor, flyer. Als Verb to frequent a place = oft besuchen, dann Betonung auf der zweiten Silbe.

prompt: adverb from FREQUENCY: not often
sentence: I go to the cinema rather ____ as the nearest one is the other side of town and not easy to get to.
plain: I go to the cinema rather rarely as the nearest one is the other side of town and not easy to get to.
note: infrequently = rarely, formeller. Vorsilbe in-, nicht un-.

prompt: adjective from FREQUENCY: not happening often
sentence: The trains are very ____ and unreliable.
plain: The trains don't run very often and are unreliable.
note: infrequent trains, visits. Nicht unfrequent.

de: aus dem Schneider sein, aus der Verantwortung entlassen sein
prompt: one word fits three phrases (1/3): free from blame or trouble
sentence: You're not off the ____ yet. The police may still want to speak to you about the robbery.
plain: You're not free from trouble yet. The police may still want to speak to you about the robbery.
note: Auch: let s.o. off the hook = jdn. davonkommen lassen. Dasselbe Wort passt in hook s.o. up und a hook.

prompt: one word fits three phrases (2/3): to connect someone to a system
sentence: I'm going to try and ____ my parents up to the Internet so they can find out what it's all about.
plain: I'm going to try and connect my parents to the Internet so they can find out what it's all about.
note: hook up to = anschließen, verbinden. Pronomen in der Mitte: hook them up.

prompt: one word fits three phrases (3/3): a curved piece of metal for hanging things
sentence: There was a ____ on the top of the pot to allow you to hang it from the ceiling.
plain: There was a metal curve on the top of the pot to allow you to hang it from the ceiling.
note: a coat hook, hook and eye = Haken und Öse.

prompt: adjective from DRINK: not safe or not pleasant to drink
sentence: This water is ____. It tastes absolutely disgusting.
plain: This water is not safe to drink. It tastes absolutely disgusting.
note: un- + drink + -able. Gegenteil: drinkable. Trinkwasser = drinking water (hier Gerundium als Adjektiv), nicht drinkable water im Schild-Sinn.

de: einer Sache ein Ende setzen, etwas beenden
prompt: to ____ an end to something: to make it stop
sentence: Demonstrators hope the Government will ____ an end to animal experimentation.
plain: Demonstrators hope the Government will stop animal experimentation.
note: put an end to + Nomen oder -ing: put an end to the rumours, to smoking. Ähnlich: put a stop to sth. Nicht verwechseln: come to an end = enden (ohne Objekt), bring sth. to an end = etwas zu Ende bringen.

prompt: to give away or sell something that you value
sentence: The watch my father left me is the one object that I could never ____ with.
plain: The watch my father left me is the one object that I could never give away.
note: part with sth. = sich von Dingen trennen, meist widerwillig: I hate parting with money. Für Personen: part from s.o. (selten), besser say goodbye to s.o. Auch: part company with s.o. = sich trennen.

prompt: adjective from EXCEPT: unusually good
sentence: She is a good athlete but I wouldn't say she's ____.
plain: She is a good athlete but I wouldn't say she's outstanding.
note: Meist positiv: exceptional talent, quality. Auch: in exceptional circumstances = unter besonderen Umständen. Gegenteil: unexceptional = durchschnittlich.

prompt: noun from EXCEPT: used to say that someone is not included
sentence: Can everyone with the ____ of Marta see me at the end of the lesson.
plain: Can everyone except Marta see me at the end of the lesson.
note: with the exception of + Nomen = außer; formeller als except oder apart from. Auch: the exception to the rule, make an exception, without exception = ausnahmslos.

prompt: adverb from EXCEPT: unusually
sentence: It's been ____ warm this summer, hasn't it?
plain: It's been unusually warm this summer, hasn't it?
note: exceptionally + Adjektiv: exceptionally good, rare, cold. Stärker als very. Schreibweise mit zwei l: exceptionally.

prompt: to ____ attention on something: to concentrate on it
sentence: I'd like you all now to ____ attention on the arguments against the proposal.
plain: I'd like you all now to concentrate on the arguments against the proposal.
note: focus (one's) attention on sth. oder kurz focus on sth. Ähnlich: draw attention to sth. = Aufmerksamkeit lenken auf, pay attention to sth. = beachten. Auch: in focus / out of focus.

term: a chip off the old block
de: ganz der Vater (die Mutter), das Ebenbild der Eltern
prompt: one word fits three phrases (with a mental block and a block of flats): a child who is very like a parent
sentence: He's like his father in so many ways and is a real chip off the old ____.
plain: He is very like his father in so many ways, with the same character.
note: a chip off the old block: ein Kind, das seinem Elternteil sehr ähnelt, meist anerkennend. Dasselbe Wort passt in a mental block und a block of flats (Wohnblock).

prompt: one word fits three phrases (with a chip off the old block and a block of flats): a sudden failure to remember or think about something
sentence: I had a complete mental ____ and couldn't remember the registration number of my car.
plain: I couldn't think properly and couldn't remember the registration number of my car.
note: have a mental block (about sth.). Auch: writer's block = Schreibblockade. Wörtlich: block = Block, Klotz, Sperre; auch das Verb block = blockieren.

de: zugunsten von jdm. gewichtet, bevorzugt (System, Regel)
prompt: adjective from WEIGH: arranged to give one group an advantage
sentence: The system is ____ in favour of those earning less than the national average.
plain: The system gives an advantage to those earning less than the national average.
note: be weighted in favour of / against / towards sth. Auch: a weighted average = gewichteter Durchschnitt. Nicht verwechseln: weighty (gewichtig), weightless (schwerelos).

prompt: adjective from WEIGH: important and serious
sentence: We discussed several ____ issues today in the discussion class.
plain: We discussed several important and serious issues today in the discussion class.
note: weighty issue, matter, decision, question; eher formell. Wörtlich auch: schwer (a weighty book). Nicht verwechseln: weighted.

prompt: adverb from UP: in the direction of a higher place
sentence: She tilted her head and gazed ____ at the stars.
plain: She tilted her head and gazed up at the stars.
note: -wards bildet Richtungsadverbien: upwards, downwards, forwards, backwards (amerikanisch oft ohne -s: upward). Nicht verwechseln: upright = aufrecht (Adjektiv). Als Adjektiv: an upward trend.

prompt: adjective from ANIMATE: not alive
sentence: Rocks, tables and chairs are ____ objects.
plain: Rocks, tables and chairs are not alive.
note: in- + animate: Gegenteil von animate = belebt. Nicht verwechseln: animated = lebhaft, auch Zeichentrick (an animated film). Romanisch fast gleich: ES/PT inanimado, IT inanimato, FR inanimé.

prompt: noun from PROXIMATE: the state of being close to something
sentence: The house is popular because of its ____ to the station.
plain: The house is popular because it is so near the station.
note: proximity to sth. = Nähe zu etwas; in close proximity = ganz in der Nähe. Endung -ity (nicht -aty). Romanisch: ES proximidad, IT prossimità, FR proximité, PT proximidade.

prompt: to feel slightly ill or unwell
sentence: I'm feeling a bit ____ the weather today, so I'll stay in bed.
plain: I'm feeling a bit unwell today, so I'll stay in bed.
note: Meist leichte Beschwerden (Erkältung, Müdigkeit), nichts Ernstes; nicht wörtlich zu verstehen. Ähnlich: be off colour, be run down. Gleiches Bild im Französischen und Russischen: FR ne pas être dans son assiette, RU не в своей тарелке (ne v svojéj tarélke), wörtlich „nicht in seinem Teller“.

de: außerdem, noch dazu, und mehr noch
prompt: used to add a further point, often a stronger one
sentence: The hotel is right on the beach and, what's ____, it costs very little.
plain: The hotel is right on the beach and also costs very little.
note: what's more / what is more leitet eine zusätzliche, oft stärkere Information ein. Nicht: what's best. Ähnlich: moreover (formeller), besides, on top of that. DE außerdem, ES es más, IT per di più, FR qui plus est, PT além disso.

prompt: adjective: lost by a very small margin
sentence: The team suffered a ____ defeat, losing by a single goal.
plain: The team lost the match by just one goal.
note: narrow passt zu defeat, victory, win, escape und margin; close passt zu contest, race, call und match. Romanisch: ES derrota por la mínima, IT sconfitta di misura, FR défaite de justesse, PT derrota por pouco.

prompt: to agree to do something, often in a formal situation
sentence: The two companies have entered ____ a partnership to develop the new engine.
plain: The two companies have formally agreed to work together to develop the new engine.
note: Formell. Typisch: enter into an agreement / a contract / negotiations / a partnership. Nicht: enter in. Gegenüber enter a room (ohne into). DE eine Vereinbarung eingehen, FR conclure un accord, IT stipulare un accordo, ES suscribir un acuerdo.

de: sich etwas stellen, etwas akzeptieren und damit umgehen
prompt: to accept and deal with a difficult situation
sentence: It is time you started ____ up to the fact that you cannot please everyone.
plain: It is time you accepted that you cannot please everyone.
note: Oft: face up to the fact that / to reality / to your responsibilities. Romanisch gleicher Aufbau im Französischen: faire face à. Sonst ES afrontar, IT affrontare, PT enfrentar, DE sich stellen.

prompt: adjective from PASS: impossible to travel on or through
sentence: After the heavy snow many mountain roads were ____ this morning.
plain: After the heavy snow it was impossible to drive on many mountain roads this morning.
note: Negativpräfix im- vor p, b, m (impossible, impatient, imbalance); nicht um- oder un-. Falsche Freunde: ES impasible und IT impassibile heißen unbewegt, ungerührt (EN impassive). Unpassierbare Straße: ES intransitable, FR infranchissable.

prompt: noun from PASS (+ by): a person who walks past
sentence: Lost in the old town, we asked a ____-by for the way to the station.
plain: Lost in the old town, we asked someone walking past for the way to the station.
note: Person = -er: passer-by, Plural passers-by (das -s steht an passer). passing = vorbeigehend, flüchtig (a passing remark). DE Passant, FR passant, IT passante, ES und PT transeúnte / transeunte.

term: get sth. out of one's system
de: sich etwas von der Seele schaffen, sich austoben, es hinter sich bringen
prompt: to do something so that you no longer feel the need to do it
sentence: She spent a whole summer partying to get it out of her ____ before starting work.
plain: She spent a whole summer partying so that she would no longer want to before starting work.
note: Informell. Einem Drang nachgeben, damit er verschwindet (Reiselust, Partys, Wut). Nicht verwechseln: get it out of your head = es sich aus dem Kopf schlagen. Ähnlich: let off steam. FR se défouler, IT sfogarsi, ES desfogarse, DE sich austoben.
alt: get it out of your system
get it out of his system
get it out of her system

de: Umzug, Prozession; auch: eine ganze Reihe von Personen
prompt: noun related to PROCESS: a line of people moving along slowly
sentence: A long ____ of pilgrims walked slowly through the village to the church.
plain: A long line of pilgrims walked slowly through the village to the church.
note: Aussprache procession [prəˈseʃn], aber process [ˈprəʊses] (BE). Übertragen: a procession of visitors = ein ständiges Kommen und Gehen. Romanisch: ES procesión, IT processione, FR procession, PT procissão.

de: Süßstoff, Süßungsmittel; informell: Anreiz in einem Geschäft
prompt: noun from SWEET: a substance used instead of sugar
sentence: Many diet drinks contain artificial ____ instead of sugar.
plain: Many diet drinks contain substances that taste sweet but are not sugar.
note: sweet + -en (süßen) + -er: sweeten, sweetener. Zählbar, daher Plural nach artificial. Informell auch: a sweetener to close the deal = ein Anreiz. ES edulcorante, IT dolcificante, FR édulcorant, PT adoçante.

prompt: phrase: one after another, without a break
sentence: She won the title four years in ____.
plain: She won the title four years in a row.
note: in succession ist ein fester Block: three times in succession, for the second year in succession. Gleichbedeutend: in a row, running. Nicht: a succession was made. a succession of + Plural = eine Reihe von. DE in Folge, ES consecutivo, IT consecutivo, FR consécutif, PT consecutivo.

prompt: people are saying that something may be true
sentence: Rumour has ____ that the old cinema will be turned into a supermarket.
plain: People say that the old cinema will be turned into a supermarket.
note: Rumour has it that + vollständiger Satz (nicht that-Satz mit Infinitiv). AmE: rumor has it. Ähnlich: word has it that. DE es heißt, ES corre el rumor de que, IT corre voce che, FR le bruit court que, PT corre o boato de que.

term: be on the verge of sth.
de: kurz davor sein, am Rande von etwas stehen
prompt: very close to doing or experiencing something
sentence: After months of talks the two countries are on the verge ____ signing a treaty.
plain: After months of talks the two countries are very close to signing a treaty.
note: on the verge of + Nomen oder -ing: on the verge of tears, of collapse, of becoming. Nicht: on the verge that oder on the verge to. Ähnlich: on the brink of, about to. FR être sur le point de, ES estar a punto de, IT essere sul punto di, PT estar prestes a.

de: jdn. überraschen, verblüffen, aus der Fassung bringen
prompt: to surprise or shock someone
sentence: I was completely taken ____ by her sudden anger.
plain: I was very surprised by her sudden anger.
note: Meist im Passiv: be taken aback (by sth.). aback gibt es praktisch nur in dieser Wendung. Nicht: taken back (= zurückgebracht). Ähnlich: be thrown, be stunned. DE verblüfft, ES desconcertar, IT spiazzare, FR décontenancer, PT surpreender.

term: keep sb. in the dark (about sth.)
de: jdn. im Unklaren lassen, nicht informieren
prompt: to not tell someone about something
sentence: Parents were kept in the ____ about the changes to the timetable.
plain: Parents were not told about the changes to the timetable.
note: Auch: be in the dark about sth. = nichts darüber wissen. Gegenteil: keep sb. in the loop / posted. DE im Dunkeln lassen, ES tener a alguien a oscuras, IT tenere all'oscuro, FR tenir dans l'ignorance.

de: auf keinen Fall, unter keinen Umständen
prompt: phrase: not for any reason (formal)
sentence: On no ____ should you open the door to strangers.
plain: You must never open the door to strangers.
note: Verneinende Wendung am Satzanfang löst Inversion aus: On no account should / must you … Formell. Ähnlich: under no circumstances, in no way. DE auf keinen Fall, ES bajo ningún concepto, IT in nessun caso, FR en aucun cas, PT em nenhuma circunstância.

prompt: phrase: sometimes, but not often
sentence: He still visits his old school on ____, usually in December.
plain: He still visits his old school sometimes, usually in December.
note: on occasion = gelegentlich. Nicht verwechseln: in the event of = im Falle von; on the occasion of = anlässlich. ES en ocasiones, IT in alcune occasioni, FR à l'occasion, PT por vezes.

prompt: to put yourself in great physical danger
sentence: Mountain rescuers risk life and ____ to reach injured climbers.
plain: Mountain rescuers put themselves in great danger to reach injured climbers.
note: Feste Paarformel: life and limb (limb = Gliedmaße). Nicht: life and bone. Andere Paare: flesh and blood, skin and bone. DE Leib und Leben, ES arriesgar la vida, IT rischiare la vita, FR risquer sa vie, PT arriscar a vida.

de: eine ganze Menge, eine Vielzahl von etwas
prompt: a very large number of things or people
sentence: The new system caused a whole ____ of problems for the staff.
plain: The new system caused many different problems for the staff.
note: a host of + Plural, oft a whole host of. Nicht verwechseln mit host = Gastgeber. Nicht: a whole scale of. Ähnlich: a whole range / raft / series of. DE eine Vielzahl von, ES una multitud de, IT una miriade di, FR une foule de, PT uma série de.

term: owe a debt of gratitude to sb.
de: jdm. zu großem Dank verpflichtet sein
prompt: to be very grateful to someone for their help
sentence: We owe a huge debt of ____ to our teachers.
plain: We are deeply grateful to our teachers for all their help.
note: Meist: a huge / great / deep debt of gratitude; eher formell. Gleiche Struktur in vielen Sprachen: DE Dankesschuld, ES deuda de gratitud, IT debito di gratitudine, FR dette de reconnaissance, PT dívida de gratidão.

prompt: extremely important; necessary
sentence: Clean water is of ____ importance for the health of the whole village.
plain: Clean water is extremely important for the health of the whole village.
note: of vital importance (to sb./sth.). Ähnlich: of great / utmost / paramount importance. Nicht: of strong importance. DE von entscheidender Bedeutung, ES de vital importancia, IT di vitale importanza, FR d'une importance vitale, PT de importância vital.

prompt: phrase: used to say that one event caused a different outcome in the past
sentence: If it hadn't been ____ your advice, I would have made a terrible mistake.
plain: Without your advice, I would have made a terrible mistake.
note: 3. Konditionalsatz (Vergangenheit): if it hadn't been for + Nomen, … would have + Partizip. Gegenwart: if it weren't for (nicht wasn't). Formell: had it not been for. DE wäre … nicht gewesen, ES de no haber sido por, IT se non fosse stato per, FR sans, PT se não fosse por.
alt: if it had not been for

term: be on good terms with sb.
de: mit jdm. gut auskommen, ein gutes Verhältnis zu jdm. haben
prompt: to have a friendly relationship with someone
sentence: We are ____ very good terms with our neighbours.
plain: We get on very well with our neighbours.
note: be on good / bad / friendly terms with sb.; auch be on first-name terms. Nicht: in good terms (Interferenz aus ES en buenos términos und FR en bons termes). Ähnlich: get on well with sb. IT essere in buoni rapporti con.
alt: be on very good terms with

de: jdm. wird die Tasche entrissen, gestohlen
prompt: have + object + past participle: something unpleasant happens to you
sentence: Sue ____ her bag snatched at the concert.
plain: Someone snatched Sue's bag at the concert.
note: have sth. done: etwas passiert jdm. (oft Unangenehmes) oder wird für jdn. erledigt. Person = robbed (Sue was robbed), Sache = stolen oder snatched. Informell auch: get your bag snatched. FR se faire voler son sac, IT farsi rubare la borsa, ES le robaron el bolso.

prompt: formal phrase: never, at no moment
sentence: At ____ time was the public in any danger.
plain: The public was never in any danger.
note: At no time + Inversion: At no time were we aware … Ähnlich: on no account, under no circumstances. Inversion gibt es in ES, IT und FR nicht: en ningún momento, in nessun momento, à aucun moment.

prompt: to be helped or improved by something
sentence: You would greatly benefit ____ a few weeks' holiday.
plain: A few weeks' holiday would be very good for you.
note: benefit from sth.; Nomen: the benefit of sth. / benefit to sb. Ähnlich: profit from. DE profitieren von, ES beneficiarse de, IT beneficiare di, FR bénéficier de, PT beneficiar de.

de: diskreditieren, in Verruf bringen, unglaubwürdig machen
prompt: verb from CREDIT: to make people stop trusting someone or something
sentence: The newspaper's story was later ____ by several independent bloggers.
plain: The newspaper's story was later shown to be untrustworthy by several independent bloggers.
note: dis- + credit; oft im Passiv. Hinweis im Text: or called into question = negatives Verb. Nicht: miscredited. dis- steht oft bei Verben (discredit, disprove, disagree). ES desacreditar, IT screditare, FR discréditer, PT desacreditar.

prompt: verb from PROVE: to show that something is not true
sentence: The scientists tried to verify the theory or, alternatively, to ____ it.
plain: The scientists tried to show that the theory was not true.
note: dis- + prove (Verb: oo wird zu o). Gegenteil von verify, confirm, prove. Nicht: proofread (= Korrektur lesen). Partizip: disproved oder disproven. DE widerlegen, ES refutar, IT confutare, FR réfuter, PT refutar.

prompt: adjective: seeming to be everywhere at the same time
sentence: Smartphones have become so ____ that few people leave home without one.
plain: Smartphones are now found everywhere, so few people leave home without one.
note: Gehobenes Wort. Nomen: ubiquity. Aussprache [juːˈbɪkwɪtəs]. Lateinisch ubique = überall. DE ubiquitär, ES ubicuo, IT ubiquo, FR ubiquité (Nomen).

prompt: adjective from CONCEIVE: possible to imagine or believe
sentence: Writers now cover every ____ subject on their blogs.
plain: Writers now cover every possible subject on their blogs.
note: conceive + -able: das e bleibt, Endung -able (nicht -ible). every conceivable + Nomen = jeder erdenkliche. Gegenteil: inconceivable. ES concebible, IT concepibile, FR concevable, PT concebível.

prompt: adverb from ELOQUENT: in a fluent and persuasive way
sentence: The mayor spoke so ____ that the whole hall fell silent.
plain: The mayor spoke so well and persuasively that the whole hall fell silent.
note: eloquence, eloquent, eloquently: -ent wird zu -ently (nicht nur -ly). Aussprache [ˈeləkwənt]. ES elocuentemente, IT eloquentemente, FR avec éloquence, PT eloquentemente.

de: etwas in etwas einbinden, integrieren, aufnehmen
prompt: verb: to include something as part of a whole
sentence: Most newspapers have now ____ blogging into their news services.
plain: Most newspapers have now included blogging in their news services.
note: incorporate sth. into sth. Nomen: incorporation. Nicht: corporate (Adjektiv: Unternehmens-). ES incorporar, IT incorporare, FR incorporer, PT incorporar, DE einbinden oder integrieren.

de: etwas abwenden, einer Sache zuvorkommen, etwas verhindern
prompt: to take action to stop something unpleasant from happening
sentence: The minister acted quickly to head ____ a possible strike.
plain: The minister acted quickly to prevent a possible strike from happening.
note: head off sth. / head sb. off = abfangen, bevor es passiert: head off criticism, a crisis, trouble. Nicht: head back (= zurückfahren) und nicht head for (= Kurs nehmen auf). DE abwenden oder zuvorkommen, ES atajar, IT prevenire, FR parer à.

de: jdn. beruhigen, jdm. die Sorge nehmen
prompt: to stop someone from worrying
sentence: The test results will ____ her mind at rest.
plain: The test results will stop her from worrying.
note: put sb.'s mind at rest (auch: at ease). Nicht: lay. lay sth. to rest beendet ein Gerücht oder einen Zweifel (lay a fear to rest). Auch set sb.'s mind at rest kommt in Wörterbüchern vor (allgemeines Wissen, nicht geprüft). DE jdn. beruhigen, ES tranquilizar a alguien, IT tranquillizzare qualcuno, FR rassurer.

de: sich mit etwas abmühen, mit etwas ringen, sich mit etwas herumschlagen
prompt: to try hard to deal with a difficult problem
sentence: Governments are still ____ with the problem of how to reduce traffic in city centres.
plain: Governments are still struggling hard to deal with the problem of how to reduce traffic in city centres.
note: grapple with a problem, an issue, a question, difficulties. Wörtlich: ringen, im Nahkampf kämpfen. Nicht: juggle (= mehrere Aufgaben unter einen Hut bringen: juggle work and family) und nicht tinker with (= herumbasteln). ES lidiar con oder bregar con, IT essere alle prese con, FR se débattre avec, DE sich herumschlagen mit.

prompt: adjective from SUSTAIN: continuing for a long time without weakening
sentence: The village came under ____ attack that lasted for three days.
plain: The village was attacked again and again for three days without a break.
note: sustained = tatsächlich lange anhaltend: sustained attack, effort, growth, pressure, period. sustainable = fortsetzbar, tragfähig, nachhaltig: sustainable growth, development. Nomen: sustainability. Verb sustain = aufrechterhalten, tragen, erleiden (sustain injuries). Bei flo-joe: see sustained economic growth. ES sostenido, IT prolungato, FR soutenu.

prompt: adjective from RESPECT: good enough, or of an acceptable standard
sentence: She finished the marathon in a very ____ time, given that she had hardly trained.
plain: She finished the marathon in a quite good time, given that she had hardly trained.
note: respect + -able. respectable = ordentlich, ansehnlich (a respectable score), auch gesellschaftlich anständig. respectful = respektvoll (Verhalten). respected = angesehen (Person). respective = jeweilig. Nicht: respecting. ES respetable, IT rispettabile, FR respectable, DE respektabel.

de: auf etwas kommen, auf etwas stoßen (Idee, Lösung)
prompt: to think of a good idea or solution, often by chance
sentence: After weeks of trying, she finally ____ on a solution to the problem.
plain: After weeks of trying, she finally found a solution to the problem by chance.
note: hit on (auch gehobener: hit upon) a solution, an idea, a way of doing sth. Nicht: strike. Mit strike ist die Idee das Subjekt: An idea struck me. It struck me that … (strike on/upon kommt in Wörterbüchern vor, ist aber selten; nicht geprüft). DE auf etwas kommen, ES dar con, FR tomber sur, IT trovare per caso.

prompt: adjective from SECRET: not willing to tell people about things
sentence: She was always very ____ about her private life and never told us anything.
plain: She was always unwilling to tell people about her private life and never told us anything.
note: secretive beschreibt eine Person (be secretive about sth.), secret die Sache (geheim), secrecy = Geheimhaltung, secretly = heimlich. Endung -ive für eine Eigenschaft. ES reservado, IT riservato, FR cachottier (umgangssprachlich).

prompt: noun from DIFFER: giving different pupils tasks at the right level
sentence: A key skill in mixed-ability classes is ____, giving each pupil tasks at the right level.
plain: A key skill in mixed-ability classes is giving each pupil tasks at the right level.
note: differentiate (between A and B) = unterscheiden; differentiation = Unterscheidung und im Unterricht Differenzierung (Binnendifferenzierung). Nicht: difference (= Unterschied). Aussprache [ˌdɪfəˌrenʃiˈeɪʃn]. ES diferenciación, IT differenziazione, FR différenciation.

prompt: noun from DIFFER: a difference in amount, especially in pay (economics)
sentence: The union is fighting to reduce the pay ____ between workers in different industries.
plain: The union is fighting to reduce the differences in pay between workers in different industries.
note: pay/wage/price/interest-rate differentials: Fachwort der Wirtschaft, meist Plural. difference ist allgemeiner. Ähnlich: pay gap. ES diferencial salarial, IT differenziale salariale, FR écart salarial.

de: jdm. etwas nachtragen, jdm. etwas übelnehmen
prompt: to think less of someone because of something they have done
sentence: I admit I made a mistake, but please don't ____ it against me.
plain: I admit I made a mistake, but please don't think badly of me for it.
note: Oft verneint: Don't hold it against me. Niveau laut Oxford Learner's Dictionaries: C2. Ähnlich: bear/hold a grudge (Groll hegen). Nicht: hold sth. over sb. (jdn. mit etwas unter Druck setzen). DE jdm. etwas nachtragen, FR en vouloir à qn, ES no me lo tengas en cuenta, IT non avercela con me.

prompt: to spend time in a relaxed way while waiting
sentence: We had a few hours before the train arrived, so we ____ away the time reading and chatting.
plain: We had a few hours before the train arrived, so we passed the time reading and chatting.
note: while away the time / the hours / an afternoon, meist mit -ing: whiled away the hours reading. Das Verb while gibt es praktisch nur in dieser Wendung. Nicht: waste (= verschwenden, abwertend). DE sich die Zeit vertreiben, ES pasar el rato oder matar el tiempo, IT ingannare il tempo, FR tuer le temps.

term: be on record as saying sth.
de: öffentlich festgehalten haben, dass; offiziell erklärt haben
prompt: formal: publicly known to have said something
sentence: The Prime Minister is on ____ as saying that unemployment will fall this year.
plain: The Prime Minister has publicly said that unemployment will fall this year.
note: be on record as saying + Nebensatz oder -ing; go on record = sich öffentlich festlegen. Unterschied: on the record = offiziell und zitierbar, off the record = inoffiziell, nicht zitierbar. Aussprache: das Nomen record [ˈrekɔːd]. DE offiziell festgehalten, ES dejar constancia, FR officiellement.

prompt: noun from CREDIBLE: the quality of being believable and trusted
sentence: She lost all ____ with her colleagues when they found out she had stolen other people's ideas.
plain: She lost the trust of her colleagues when they found out she had stolen other people's ideas.
note: credible = glaubwürdig, plausibel; credibility = Glaubwürdigkeit (lose, gain, damage credibility); incredible = unglaublich. Nicht: credit (= Kredit, Anerkennung), credulity (= Leichtgläubigkeit), incredulous (= ungläubig, Person). ES credibilidad, IT credibilità, FR crédibilité.

prompt: adjective from PREPARE: done in order to get ready for something
sentence: The two leaders held a ____ meeting before the summit.
plain: The two leaders held a meeting to get ready for the summit.
note: preparatory + Nomen: meeting, talks, work, course, stage. Formal. Endung -ory (wie compulsory). Aussprache BrE [prɪˈpærətri]. preparatory to + Nomen oder -ing = vor, als Vorbereitung auf (sehr formal). preparative gibt es nur als Fachwort (Chemie). Niveau: B2 bis C1, die Quellen sind uneinheitlich. ES preparatorio, IT preparatorio, FR préparatoire.

prompt: adjective from PROTECT: giving protection, or wanting to keep someone safe
sentence: Workers on the building site must wear ____ clothing and a helmet.
plain: Workers on the building site must wear clothing that gives them protection, and a helmet.
note: protective clothing/equipment = Schutzkleidung; protective towards sb. = beschützend, fürsorglich; overprotective = überfürsorglich. Nomen protection, Partizip protected (a protected species = geschützte Art). ES protector, IT protettivo, FR protecteur.

prompt: to be judged in a court of law
sentence: He will stand ____ on charges of fraud and corruption.
plain: He will go to court, accused of fraud and corruption.
note: stand trial (for sth.), be on trial, put sb. on trial. Dasselbe Wort passt auch in trial period (Probezeit) und trial and error (Versuch und Irrtum). Nicht: process (= Vorgang). ES ser juzgado, IT essere processato, FR être jugé.

prompt: formal: to look or be similar to someone or something
sentence: The modern monarchy ____ even less resemblance to the original pattern.
plain: The modern monarchy looks even less like the original pattern.
note: bear (a) resemblance to; meist mit little/no/some/a striking: bears little resemblance to. Vergangenheit: bore. Nicht: get oder make. FR présenter une ressemblance avec, ES guardar parecido con, IT avere somiglianza con.

de: sich abwechseln mit, im Wechsel auftreten mit
prompt: to follow one after the other in a repeated pattern
sentence: Periods of heavy rain alternate ____ long dry spells.
plain: Periods of heavy rain follow long dry spells, again and again.
note: A alternates with B = A und B wechseln sich ab. Auch alternate between A and B. Nicht: from oder by. FR alterner avec, ES alternar con, IT alternarsi con. Achtung: alternate ist auch ein Adjektiv (alternate days = jeden zweiten Tag).

prompt: worthy of being noticed because of a particular quality
sentence: The cathedral is remarkable ____ its stunning Gothic architecture.
plain: The cathedral is worth noticing because of its stunning Gothic architecture.
note: remarkable for + Nomen/-ing (Grund, wofür etwas auffällt). Nicht: by oder of. FR remarquable par, ES notable por, IT notevole per. Falle: Im Deutschen sagt man oft durch.

prompt: the freedom to change your plans or actions
sentence: In a negotiation you should always leave yourself some ____ for manoeuvre.
plain: In a negotiation you should always keep some freedom to change your plans.
note: room for manoeuvre = Spielraum (BrE manoeuvre, AmE maneuver). Auch: little/no/plenty of room for manoeuvre, limited room for manoeuvre. Nicht: space oder scope. FR marge de manœuvre, ES margen de maniobra, IT margine di manovra.

prompt: noun from ACT: the state of doing nothing
sentence: A long period of ____ on the bulletin board led the company to think that the website was getting very few visitors.
plain: A long period of doing nothing on the bulletin board led the company to think the website had few visitors.
note: in- verneint: active, inactive; activity, inactivity. Nicht: inaction (= Nichthandeln, bewusstes Nichtstun) und nicht activity (Gegenteil). FR inactivité, ES inactividad, IT inattività.

prompt: adjective from ACT: allowing two-way communication between a user and a system
sentence: We have bought a fantastic ____ TV. You can programme it and take part in live competitions.
plain: We have bought a fantastic TV that lets you take part in live competitions.
note: inter- = zwischen, miteinander: interact, interaction, interactive. Nicht: reactive (reagierend) oder active. FR interactif, ES interactivo, IT interattivo.

prompt: verb from ACT: to start something working
sentence: When we have confirmation that your payment has been received, your account will be ____.
plain: When we have confirmation that your payment has arrived, we will switch your account on.
note: activate = aktivieren, freischalten; passiv: will be activated. reactivate nur, wenn es vorher schon aktiv war. Verbendung -ate. FR activé, ES activado, IT attivato.

prompt: one word fits: receive money, a problem or a quality from someone before you
sentence: A distant cousin of mine ____ a fortune when his father died.
plain: A distant cousin of mine was left a fortune when his father died.
note: inherit a fortune / a house / a problem / a talent / a trait. Nomen inheritance = Erbe, Erbschaft. Nicht: heir (= Erbe, Person). Vergleich: DE erben, FR hériter, ES heredar, IT ereditare.

de: (viel) Geld hinblättern, tief in die Tasche greifen
prompt: informal: to pay a lot of money for something, often unwillingly
sentence: Many nurses have to ____ out huge chunks of their income on rent.
plain: Many nurses have to spend huge chunks of their income on rent.
note: fork out (for/on sth.), informell. Oft mit huge chunks / a fortune / a lot. Ähnlich: shell out, cough up. FR casquer, ES soltar la pasta, IT sborsare.

de: über die Runden kommen, mit dem Geld auskommen
prompt: to earn just enough money to live on
sentence: Many families struggle to make ____ meet.
plain: Many families struggle to get by on their wages.
note: make ends meet, auch make both ends meet (BrE). Oft mit struggle/find it hard to. Nicht: make means. FR joindre les deux bouts, ES llegar a fin de mes, IT sbarcare il lunario.

term: get a foot on the housing ladder
de: den Einstieg in den Immobilienmarkt schaffen, die erste Immobilie kaufen
prompt: to buy your first home
sentence: Young people find it hard to get a foot on the housing ____.
plain: Young people find it hard to buy their first home.
note: get a foot on the housing/property ladder. Beide Varianten sind üblich, im Text steht housing ladder. FR mettre un pied sur l'échelle immobilière, ES acceder a la vivienda en propiedad, IT comprare la prima casa.
alt: get a foot on the housing ladder
get a foot on the property ladder

de: sich etwas nicht mehr leisten können (wegen der Preise), verdrängt werden
prompt: to be unable to afford something because the price has risen too much
sentence: Many residents are being ____ out of the more desirable areas.
plain: Many residents can no longer afford the more desirable areas.
note: be priced out of + Ort/Markt, meist Passiv. Aktiv: rising rents price people out of the area. Nicht: paid out. DE verdrängt werden (durch Preise).

prompt: to make prices, costs or demand rise
sentence: Wealthy foreign buyers ____ up property prices.
plain: Wealthy foreign buyers make property prices rise.
note: drive up prices/costs/demand, Gegenteil: bring down. Das Muster ist drive + Nomen + up oder drive up + Nomen. Auch möglich: push up. FR faire grimper, ES disparar, IT far salire.

prompt: to move or change at the same speed as something
sentence: Wages have not kept ____ with rising house prices.
plain: Wages have not risen as fast as house prices.
note: keep pace with sb./sth. (meist verneint oder mit struggle to). Nicht: keep speed. Ähnlich: keep up with. FR suivre le rythme de, ES seguir el ritmo de, IT stare al passo con.

prompt: to remember a fact when you make a decision
sentence: We should ____ in mind that not all migrants are wealthy.
plain: We should remember that not all migrants are wealthy.
note: bear sth. in mind / bear in mind that. Auch bearing in mind that = angesichts der Tatsache, dass. Nicht: take in mind. Ähnlich: keep in mind. FR garder à l'esprit, ES tener en cuenta, IT tenere a mente.

prompt: a result that causes further, often unplanned, results
sentence: Delayed independence has ____-on implications for birth rates.
plain: Delayed independence has further consequences for birth rates.
note: knock-on effect/implications/consequences. Adjektiv, immer mit Bindestrich vor dem Nomen. Nicht: follow-on. FR effet domino, ES efecto dominó, IT effetto a catena.

prompt: verb: to make a problem or bad situation worse
sentence: The shortage is further ____ by the arrival of newcomers.
plain: The shortage is made worse by the arrival of newcomers.
note: exacerbate a problem/situation/tensions; oft im Passiv: exacerbated by. Formell. Nicht: exaggerate (= übertreiben). FR aggraver, ES agravar, IT esacerbare.

prompt: to offer more money than someone else for something
sentence: Wealthy foreign buyers are able to ____ local residents.
plain: Wealthy foreign buyers are able to offer more money than local residents.
note: outbid sb. (for sth.). Unregelmäßig: outbid, outbid, outbid. Gegenstück: underbid. Nicht: overbid (= zu viel bieten). FR surenchérir, ES pujar más que, IT superare l'offerta di.

prompt: used to say that something is obvious
sentence: It goes without ____ that more people need more housing.
plain: It is obvious that more people need more housing.
note: it goes without saying that + Satz. Formell bis neutral. Nicht: goes without telling. FR cela va sans dire, ES ni que decir tiene, IT va da sé.

prompt: to happen or develop in a particular way
sentence: The crisis ____ out differently from country to country.
plain: The crisis develops differently from country to country.
note: play out = (sich) entwickeln; oft mit differently/in different ways. Nicht: work out (= klappen, ausrechnen). FR se dérouler, ES desarrollarse, IT svolgersi.

de: auf andere Gedanken kommen, sich ablenken von
prompt: to stop thinking about a worry for a while
sentence: A long walk helped her take her ____ off the exam results.
plain: A long walk helped her stop thinking about the exam results.
note: take your/her/his mind off sth.; oft mit help/try to. Nicht: take your thoughts off. FR se changer les idées, ES distraerse, IT distrarsi.

prompt: different rules for different people, which is unfair
sentence: The company has been accused of applying double ____ to men and women.
plain: The company has been accused of applying two different sets of rules to men and women.
note: double standards (meist Plural), auch a double standard. Nicht: double morals. FR deux poids, deux mesures, ES doble rasero, IT doppio standard (auch doppia morale).

prompt: adjective from ACCUSTOMED: not used to something
sentence: I am ____ to speaking in public, so I felt very nervous.
plain: I am not used to speaking in public, so I felt very nervous.
note: be unaccustomed to + -ing / Nomen; Gegenteil: be accustomed to. Das Präfix ist un-, nicht in-. Auch: unaccustomed (= ungewohnt) in an unaccustomed silence. FR inhabituel, ES desacostumbrado, IT non abituato.

prompt: adjective from CUSTOM: normal or traditional in a particular situation
sentence: It is ____ to bring a small gift when you are invited to dinner.
plain: It is normal to bring a small gift when you are invited to dinner.
note: customary = üblich; it is customary to + Verb. Verwandt: custom (Brauch), customs (Zoll), customer (Kunde), accustomed (gewohnt). Nicht: costume (Kostüm). Formell. FR coutumier, ES habitual, IT consueto.

prompt: adjective from INHABIT: good enough to live in
sentence: The old farmhouse was barely ____ after the storm.
plain: The old farmhouse was barely fit to live in after the storm.
note: habitable = bewohnbar; uninhabitable = unbewohnbar; inhabited = bewohnt. Endung -able = kann. Nicht: habitual (= gewohnheitsmäßig). FR habitable, ES habitable, IT abitabile.

de: kurz, flüchtig, nur einen Augenblick dauernd
prompt: adjective from MOMENT: lasting for a very short time
sentence: A ____ lapse in concentration cost him the match.
plain: A very brief lapse in concentration cost him the match.
note: momentary = kurz, flüchtig (momentary lapse/pause/silence). Nicht: momentous (= bedeutsam). Endung -ary. ES momentáneo, IT momentaneo, FR momentané.

prompt: adjective from MOMENT: very important, with serious effects
sentence: It was a ____ decision with wide-ranging consequences for the whole town.
plain: It was a very important decision with wide-ranging consequences for the whole town.
note: momentous = bedeutsam (momentous decision/occasion/event). Endung -ous. Nicht: momentary (= kurz). ES trascendental, IT di grande importanza, FR capital.

prompt: adverb from MOMENT: for a very short time
sentence: He was ____ lost for words when she walked in.
plain: For a short moment he was lost for words when she walked in.
note: momentarily = einen Augenblick lang (momentarily distracted/speechless). AmE auch: in einem Moment, gleich. Nicht: momently (veraltet). ES momentáneamente, IT momentaneamente, FR momentanément.

prompt: adjective from OBSERVE: good at noticing things
sentence: Few people are as ____ as she is; she notices every detail.
plain: Few people notice as much as she does; she sees every detail.
note: observant = aufmerksam (Adjektiv auf -ant). observer = Beobachter (Person, -er), observation = Beobachtung. Nicht: observing. ES observador, IT attento, FR observateur.

prompt: noun from REMOVE: the act of taking something away, or moving house
sentence: We hired a ____ company to take our furniture to the new house.
plain: We hired a firm to take our furniture to the new house.
note: removal = Entfernung; BrE removal company/van = Umzugsfirma (AmE moving company). Nomen auf -al aus Verben auf -ve: remove, approve, arrive. ES mudanza, IT trasloco, FR déménagement.

term: mark (the occasion / the end of an era)
prompt: one word fits: to celebrate an event, to leave a stain, to show a change
sentence: They ____ the occasion with a party in her honour.
plain: They celebrated the occasion with a party in her honour.
note: mark the occasion (den Anlass feiern); mark the end of an era (das Ende kennzeichnen); mark a surface (Flecken machen). Ein Verb, drei Bedeutungen. Nicht: draw. FR marquer, ES marcar, IT segnare.

prompt: used to say that you are happy for someone to do something
sentence: If you need help getting to the airport, by all ____ call me.
plain: If you need help getting to the airport, please do call me.
note: by all means = aber gern, ja bitte (Zustimmung). Nicht verwechseln: by no means (= keineswegs), by any means (= irgendwie). ES por supuesto, IT prego, FR bien sûr.

prompt: adjective from ADVISE: not a good idea, likely to cause problems
sentence: It is ____ to eat a heavy meal before taking exercise.
plain: It is not a good idea to eat a heavy meal before taking exercise.
note: inadvisable (nicht: unadvisable). in- bei lateinisch geprägten Adjektiven auf -able/-ible: inadvisable, inaccessible, inevitable. un- bei germanischen Stämmen: unhappy, unfinished. DE unratsam, ES desaconsejable, IT sconsigliabile, FR déconseillé.

prompt: adjective from ADVISE: giving advice or support
sentence: I work in an ____ capacity for the local Chamber of Commerce.
plain: I work as an adviser to the local Chamber of Commerce.
note: in an advisory capacity = in beratender Funktion; advisory board/role. Person: advisor oder adviser (beides korrekt, AmE eher advisor). ES asesor/consultivo, IT consultivo, FR consultatif.

prompt: to catch an illness
sentence: The game was cancelled as many players had gone ____ with influenza.
plain: The game was cancelled as many players had caught influenza.
note: go down with + Krankheit (BrE); auch come down with, in AmE häufiger. Nicht: fall down with. ES caer enfermo de, IT prendersi, FR attraper.

prompt: to sell to the highest bidder
sentence: The family announced they'd be auctioning ____ some of their art collection.
plain: The family announced they would sell some of their art collection to the highest bidder.
note: auction off sth. / auction sth. off (trennbar); off betont das Weggeben/Verkaufen. Auch: sell off. ES subastar, IT mettere all'asta, FR vendre aux enchères.

prompt: one word fits: be the same as, equal, and suit each other
sentence: They're such a well ____ couple.
plain: They are a very well suited couple.
note: match = (1) übereinstimmen: The blood matched that found at the scene. (2) gleichkommen: Profits matched those of our rivals. (3) well matched couple = gut zusammenpassend. ES coincidir/igualar, IT corrispondere, FR correspondre.
